title: A malformed agent JSON degrades the roster silently -- warning log only, HTTP 200, no runtime surface
repro: Corrupt or schema-violate any file in sidecar/agents/ (e.g. a defaultProvider the enum omits, per COD-10). _discover_specs logs 'agent <file>: schema violation ...' and continues; _specs is built once at module import (agent_runtime.py:280) so nothing re-checks. GET /agents returns 200 with 12 entries instead of 13; the only detector in the repo is the CI count assertion (tests/test_agent_runtime.py:95, tests/test_agents_router.py:41).
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:250, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:256, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:280, sidecar/routers/agents.py:68, sidecar/tests/test_agent_runtime.py:95
notes: Partial-load resilience is the right call; the missing half is the report. A user whose picker lost an agent has no way to learn why, and the packaged app has no runtime signal at all -- CLAUDE.md's own deferred item asks the smoke test to verify '/agents count > 0' for exactly this reason. Smallest fix: keep the skipped filenames + reasons in a module-level list and expose them on GET /agents (or /health) as a `degraded` field.

Worse than stated: a missing agents dir returns {} with no log at all (:237-238), which is exactly the shape of the packaged-app 'agents/ silently unavailable for 3 releases' incident CLAUDE.md records.

title: Run history is in-memory, capped at 32, and the documented list order is wrong
repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python: put three results, backtest_store.list_runs() returns them oldest-first (insertion order) while the route that serves them documents 'newest first'; get() calls move_to_end, so after any read the order is neither insertion nor recency. Separately: restart the sidecar, or run a 33rd backtest, and backtest_summary(run_id=<older run>) returns `no cached backtest with run_id=...` — the Strategy Critic can no longer critique a run the user is still looking at in the panel.
evidence: sidecar/services/backtest_store.py:23 (DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 32), sidecar/services/backtest_store.py:31 (plain OrderedDict, no disk), sidecar/services/backtest_store.py:47-48 (list returns insertion order), sidecar/services/backtest_store.py:41-45 (get mutates the order), sidecar/routers/backtest.py:176 ('List run ids currently in the in-memory cache (newest first)'), docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/CODE_PARTITION.json (subsystem responsibility says 'persisted run history')
notes: Two defects in one 70-line module: a documented contract the code contradicts (APOSD 15) and a persistence promise the implementation never made. The module is also the subsystem's shallowest (four one-line module functions over an OrderedDict, :57-70). Smallest fix: `return list(reversed(self._items.values()))` for the order; for durability, write results as JSON under the sidecar data dir keyed by run_id, which also makes the agent path in COD-backtest-7 reloadable after a restart.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: list() returns OrderedDict order (oldest-first, reshuffled to LRU by get()), contradicting the route's 'newest first' docstring, and results live only in a 32-entry in-memory cache, so backtest_summary loses runs on restart or eviction. The module docstring discloses in-memory as a deliberate v0.5.0 choice, but the Critic-loses-the-run consequence stands.

title: No timeout or AbortSignal anywhere in the shared client; the 120 s readiness budget is only checked between probes, and the Rust 'port 0 = no sidecar' sentinel is probed as a real port
repro: design: resolveAndAwaitReady awaits fetch('/health') with no signal (sidecar-client.ts:131); `Date.now() > deadline` (:138) runs only after that fetch settles, so one probe against a socket that accepts but never answers (event loop blocked by a cold model load / _MEI extraction) holds the shared readyPromise — and every panel awaiting it — for as long as the engine allows. sidecarGet (:194) likewise takes no signal, so an unmounted panel cannot cancel and a hung route is an eternal spinner. Port-0: Rust documents `0` as 'no sidecar bound this launch — the frontend treats that as disconnected' (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:273-279, :201-204) but resolvePortToBaseUrl builds http://127.0.0.1:0 unconditionally (sidecar-client.ts:97-98), so the client spends the full 120 s probing an unbindable port and then reports 'did not become ready in time'; each later caller re-arms another 120 s.
evidence: src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:125-144, src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:154-158,194-196, src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:226-234 (validateProvider: no timeout either; Ollama validate can stall on a cold daemon), src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:97-98, src-tauri/src/lib.rs:201-204,273-279
notes: A bounded-wait promise whose bound the structure does not enforce. Smallest fix: `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)` on the health probe; an optional `signal` param on sidecarGet/the new sidecarRequest with a generous default timeout. Port-0: `if (port === 0) throw new SidecarError(503, 'The data engine could not start (no free port / spawn failed). Restart Vysted.')` before the probe loop.

refuter.reason: Holds: the /health probe fetch has no signal and the deadline is checked only after it settles; sidecarGet takes no signal; resolvePortToBaseUrl builds http://127.0.0.1:0 unconditionally although Rust documents 0 as 'no sidecar bound' and start_main_sidecar returns early for port 0.

title: sidecarStatus is a one-shot boot latch: connectSidecar runs once, nothing re-probes, so the header stays green 'Connected' on a dead engine and the retry hook's documented 're-arm on reconnect' can fire at most once per app lifetime
repro: design + grep: `grep -rn 'connectSidecar\|sidecarStatus:' src plugins` -> the only caller is src/app/page.tsx:52 (mount effect) and the only writers are src/store/app.ts:25,29,32. No interval, no focus/visibility re-probe, no write from sidecarGet/streaming failures, and Rust drops the child's Terminated event (finding 8). So (a) after the sidecar dies the status chip keeps `bg-positive` + 'Connected' while every panel and the chat fail with 'Load failed'; (b) if boot lands in 'error' (120 s budget lapsed on a slow cold extraction) there is no control that calls connectSidecar again — reload is the only way out; (c) useRetryOnSidecarReady's mechanism #2 ('a fresh connecting|error -> connected transition re-runs the load') is a transition the code emits once: a panel opened after boot never sees it, and the StatusChrome provider probe keyed on it (StatusChrome.tsx:104-106) likewise never re-runs.
evidence: src/store/app.ts:24-34, src/app/page.tsx:45-52, src/lib/use-sidecar-retry.ts:19-22,113-135 (contract depends on repeated transitions), src/components/StatusChrome.tsx:173,203-210,217-220 (chip is a plain span, no retry), src/components/StatusChrome.tsx:88-106, src-tauri/src/lib.rs:226-238
notes: A status whose name promises liveness but whose structure is a boot-time boolean; two consumers (the hook's re-arm, the provider-ready probe) were designed against the promise, not the implementation — an unknown-unknown for the next maintainer, and for the owner a green light over a dead engine (truth-in-status is this product's whole pitch). Smallest fix: make the error layer the writer — sidecarGet/consumeSseStream set sidecarStatus='error' (and null readyPromise) on a connection-level failure and 'connected' on any success — plus a click-to-reconnect on the chip calling connectSidecar(); a 15-30 s /health heartbeat is the belt to that brace. Then finding 9's predicate can simply be `sidecarStatus !== 'connected'`.

refuter.reason: Holds: connectSidecar's only caller is the page mount effect (page.tsx:52) and app.ts is the only writer of sidecarStatus; no heartbeat, focus re-probe or failure-path write, so the status latches after boot and the retry hook's 're-arm on reconnect' edge fires at most once.

title: The debounced layout autosave has no flush on close, so a rearrange followed by quit within 1.5 s is lost
repro: Drag a panel to a new split, then press Cmd+Q within 1.5 s. onDidLayoutChange armed a 1500 ms timer (PanelHost.tsx:187-193); the webview dies before it fires, and nothing flushes a pending save: `grep -rn 'beforeunload|visibilitychange|pagehide|CloseRequested' src src-tauri/src` returns nothing. The cleanup (PanelHost.tsx:200-203) clears the timer instead of running it.
evidence: src/components/PanelHost.tsx:12-13,187-193,200-210
notes: Debounce without a flush converts 'coalesce writes' into 'drop the last write'. It is most visible exactly when the user tidies the cockpit before quitting. Smallest fix: keep a `pending` flag; on cleanup and on window pagehide / Tauri onCloseRequested, if pending, call autosaveLayout() immediately (fire-and-forget fetch with keepalive:true).

refuter.reason: Confirmed. onDidLayoutChange arms a 1500 ms timer, and cleanup clears it rather than flushing it. No beforeunload, pagehide, visibilitychange or onCloseRequested handler exists anywhere in src or src-tauri/src, so a layout change made in the 1.5 s before quit is lost.

title: PanelHost mounts and restores as soon as first-party modules register, before plugin modules exist, so any plugin panel in the saved layout deterministically trips the restore-failure path
repro: page.tsx:50 registers first-party modules synchronously; bootstrapPlugins (page.tsx:85-92) appends plugin modules only after awaiting persistence, getSidecarBaseUrl and each loadPlugin (plugin-bootstrap.ts:220-270). PanelHost's gate is `modules.length === 0` (PanelHost.tsx:214), so DockviewReact mounts and restoreLastSessionOrDefault runs first. If the autosave layout has a plugin panel, layoutReferencesUnknownComponent is true, so the default layout loads and deserializeWorkspace is skipped (workspace.ts:509-514). That is COD-workspace-layout-4 (non-layout state not restored, then overwritten by the next autosave), triggered on every launch. Latent today: no bundled plugin sets contributesPanels:true (plugins/*/index.ts).
evidence: src/app/page.tsx:50,85-92, src/components/PanelHost.tsx:121-126,214-226, src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:220-270, src/lib/workspace.ts:509-514
notes: Temporal coupling hidden behind a readiness proxy. 'modules registered' is used as 'all panel components known', which stops being true the moment the plugin contract's panel capability is used, and the kept plugin system exists for that. Smallest fix: gate the restore on a `pluginsReady` flag set when bootstrapPlugins resolves (with a timeout fallback), or have restore defer unknown-component panels rather than abandoning the whole blob (the COD-workspace-layout-4 fix).

refuter.reason: Confirmed as latent. registerModules runs synchronously before PanelHost mounts, while bootstrapPlugins appends plugin modules only after async persistence and loadPlugin awaits. restoreLastSessionOrDefault drops to the default layout when any component is unknown. Every surviving plugin (yfinance, vysted-news, vysted-lenses, openbb-mcp, example) sets contributesPanels:false, so nothing triggers it today; it fires the moment a panel-contributing plugin exists.

title: The India boot seed runs twice, concurrently, from two unrelated code paths
repro: design; on an IN-region boot start_warm_fundamentals schedules _boot_seed() AND _sweep_loop runs seed_india_store() on its first cycle behind a local `seeded` flag. Nothing coordinates them.
evidence: sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:416-424, sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:203-208, sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:107-152
notes: Temporal decomposition + duplicated truth. Every IN boot builds the 5k-symbol india-all row list and loads/decompresses the bundled seed pack TWICE, concurrently, with both calls contending fundamentals_store._lock. It is idempotent (NULL-fill only), so not wrong data — just doubled boot cost on the path whose whole justification is '<1 s, local-only' (:112-113), and a reader who cannot tell which path is authoritative. Smallest fix: delete the `seeded` flag and the seed call from _sweep_loop; start_warm_fundamentals already owns it.

refuter.reason: Real: on an IN boot, start_warm_fundamentals schedules _boot_seed (fundamentals_warm.py:416-424), and _sweep_loop independently calls seed_india_store on its first IN cycle behind a local flag (:197-208). The row build and the seed-pack load therefore run twice. Both are idempotent NULL-fills serialized on the store lock, and both run off-loop (asyncio.to_thread), so the only cost is duplicated background boot work nobody sees: medium -> low.

title: Crawl cycle gathers without return_exceptions and writes to the store outside the per-symbol guard
repro: design; a sqlite failure in upsert_info (line 362, outside the try at 344-361) propagates out of _one, aborts asyncio.gather (line 366, no return_exceptions=True), discards the `fetched` count, and leaves the sibling coroutines' exceptions unretrieved.
evidence: sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:362, sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:366, sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:344-361
notes: The per-symbol try carefully distinguishes a throttle from a genuine absence (:351-355) and shrugs off fetch failures — then the store write, the one call that can fail for an unrelated reason (see COD-fundamentals-profile-2), sits outside it. _crawl_loop catches the escape at :382 and logs at DEBUG, so the whole cycle silently reports fetched=0 and the operator sees a stalled crawler with no signal. Smallest fix: move the upsert inside the try and pass return_exceptions=True.

refuter.reason: Real: upsert_info at :362 sits outside the per-symbol try (:344-361), and gather at :366 has no return_exceptions. A store error therefore escapes, _crawl_loop logs it at DEBUG with fetched=0 (:378-384), and sibling coroutines keep running with unretrieved exceptions. It only triggers on a sqlite write failure, which is rare in normal use (the cited trigger, finding 2, is hypothetical), so medium -> low.

The double read is duplicated truth as well as waste: bootstrap re-derives installed/enabled from a config loadPlugin is about to load again, and the two derive different defaults (row.entry.preinstalled vs true). Fix: give sidecarGet/sidecarPost an AbortSignal.timeout ceiling, and pass the already-loaded PluginPersistedConfig into loadPlugin instead of re-fetching it.

title: The web_search hot path's documented 'instant in-process read, no network probe' actually awaits a full docker derivation on the first search of every process
repro: design (code read): web_search.py:88 calls manager.ready_base_url_detected(), whose first invocation per process awaits refresh() -> detect() ('docker version', 15s budget) + _container_status() ('docker inspect') + _container_port() ('docker port') + _health_once() (5s HTTP). With a wedged dockerd each CLI call rides the 124-timeout path at searxng_manager.py:148-153. The two comments describing this call claim the opposite.
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/web_search.py:11, sidecar/services/agent_tools/web_search.py:85, sidecar/services/agent_tools/web_search.py:88, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:337, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:348, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:91, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:97
notes: Comments-describe-non-obvious, inverted: the module docstring (web_search.py:11-13) and the inline comment (web_search.py:85-86) BOTH assert 'an instant in-process read, no network probe on the hot path', so anyone profiling a slow first research run is actively misdirected away from the cost. Concrete consequence: the first web_search after every sidecar launch -- the first research run the user sees after starting the app -- can stall tens of seconds inside one agent tool step with no progress signal. Second defect in the same function: _hot_path_detected is set to True BEFORE the await (searxng_manager.py:348-349), so a concurrent first search reads the stale None and floors to keyless while the derivation is still in flight, i.e. the run that paid for the probe may not benefit from it. Smallest fix: correct both comments; kick the one-shot derivation off in the app lifespan startup and keep the hot path on the pure ready_base_url() read the comments already promise. If it must stay lazy, set the flag after the await under the existing self._lock.

refuter.reason: Real: both comments promise an instant read with no network probe (web_search.py:10-11, :85-86), but the first call per process awaits refresh() -> docker version/inspect/port plus a 5s health probe (searxng_manager.py:337-353, :412-446). The flag is also set before the await (:348-349). Corrected on magnitude: a wedged daemon costs at most one ~15s `docker version` timeout, because code 124 means daemon_running=False and refresh returns early (searxng_manager.py:361-371, :420-431). A healthy Docker is sub-second and no CLI returns 127 immediately, so 'tens of seconds' is overstated. A concurrent first search that reads the stale None falls back to keyless and does not fail.

title: The SearXNG setup background task has no exception boundary and the module's logger is declared but never used
repro: design (code read): begin_setup fires asyncio.create_task(self.setup()) at searxng_manager.py:483; setup() catches only asyncio.CancelledError (searxng_manager.py:491). Inside _setup_locked, pick_port's RuntimeError IS guarded (:532-536) but write_settings on the line immediately above (:531) can raise OSError (unwritable data dir, full disk) uncaught -- the task dies with an unretrieved exception while state is STATE_PULLING, and `grep -n '_log' sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py` shows the logger at :62 is never called anywhere in the 656-line module.
evidence: sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:483, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:491, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:531, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:532, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:62
notes: One code path in a guarded sequence is unguarded while its immediate sibling is guarded -- the classic 'five siblings have it, this one does not'. Concrete consequence: the guided one-click setup dies, the next refresh() re-derives to 'docker_present_not_setup' (searxng_manager.py:434-437) with reason=None, and the user sees 'SearXNG is not set up yet' forever with no error, no CTA that helps, and -- because the logger is dead -- not one line anywhere explaining why. The status payload's `reason` field is the ONLY diagnostic surface this state machine has, and this path cannot populate it. Smallest fix: wrap _setup_locked's body in `except Exception as exc: self._set(STATE_ERROR, reason=...); _log.exception(...)`, and actually use _log at every docker non-zero exit.

refuter.reason: Real: setup() catches only CancelledError (searxng_manager.py:486-493). write_settings (mkdir/write_text, :227-240) runs unguarded at :531 while its sibling pick_port is guarded (:532-536). grep confirms _log (:62) is never called. Severity lowered: the trigger is an unwritable or full app data dir, and every SQLite store in the sidecar shares that dir and would fail first. The one-click flow does not hit this in normal use.

title: The managed-SearXNG error state is sticky per-process, so fixing the world by hand can never clear it and the hot path stays on keyless forever
repro: design (code read): refresh() returns the snapshot untouched whenever self.state == STATE_ERROR (searxng_manager.py:413-414), before any docker probe. Only setup()/begin_setup() or teardown() clears it (searxng_manager.py:604-607). A user whose setup failed (e.g. docker daemon was down), who then starts Docker and runs `docker start vysted-searxng` themselves, keeps state=error: the status poll never re-derives, ready_base_url() returns None, and web_search.py:88-92 floors every search to keyless.
evidence: sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:413, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:604, sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:333, sidecar/services/agent_tools/web_search.py:88
notes: The stickiness is deliberate and documented (searxng_manager.py:403-409): the status poll is the only surface that can deliver an error reason for a background setup task, so re-deriving would erase it on the first poll. But the fix scopes the error to the PROCESS rather than to the attempt, so a world change can never clear it. Concrete consequence: a running, healthy managed container is silently bypassed for the life of the sidecar -- the exact 'green in settings but unused' disease ready_base_url_detected was added to cure (searxng_manager.py:341-345), reintroduced through the other door. Smallest fix: keep the error alongside the derived state (a `last_error` field the snapshot carries) rather than AS the state, so refresh() can re-derive ready while the UI still shows what failed.

refuter.reason: Mechanism confirmed: refresh() returns early on STATE_ERROR (searxng_manager.py:413-414), so a container fixed by hand is bypassed. Severity lowered and 'forever' refuted: the error state renders 'Setup failed: <reason>' with a Retry CTA (SettingsPanel.tsx:866-867, :916-920). Retry runs setup(), which handles an already-running container straight to READY (searxng_manager.py:506-509, :560-565), and a process restart also clears it.

title: _load_master catches only FileNotFoundError/ModuleNotFoundError, so a garbled master 500s every resolve despite a docstring promising a degrade
repro: A truncated or corrupt bundled JSON (a partial PyInstaller _MEI extraction is the realistic path) makes json.load raise json.JSONDecodeError, which is not in the except tuple. Because the loaders are @lru_cache'd, the exception is never cached -- it re-raises on EVERY call -- and routers/resolve.py has no try/except, so GET /resolve returns a 500 (surfacing in the webview as a CORS error, per the repo's own CORS-masks-500 gotcha) instead of an honest no-match.
evidence: sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:373, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:374, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:313, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:266, sidecar/routers/resolve.py:93
notes: Define errors out of existence: _india_sector_map's docstring states 'a missing/garbled map degrades to {} so resolution never depends on the sector data' -- the MISSING half is true, the GARBLED half is not. The invariant is held by a comment where a two-word edit to the except tuple would hold it structurally. Smallest fix: add json.JSONDecodeError (or ValueError, OSError) to the except at :374.

refuter.reason: Mechanism confirmed: the except tuple catches only FileNotFoundError/ModuleNotFoundError, lru_cache never caches a raised exception, the resolve router has no try/except, and app.py registers a handler only for ProviderError, so a JSONDecodeError would 500 on every call and contradict the 'missing/garbled degrades to {}' docstring. Downgraded because the only trigger is a corrupt bundled master that is read-only in the package, and a truncated onefile extraction fails PyInstaller's own archive decompression before this code runs. This is a docstring-vs-code correctness gap, not a defect hit in normal use.

title: 'Durable' is row-deep: no startup reconciliation and the checkpoint is written only at exit, so a restart leaves zombie `running` rows that cannot be resumed
repro: Launch a run, call run_manager.shutdown() (what the lifespan does) -> row stays status=running forever (scratch proof P6). On a crash / kill -9 / power loss the row is `running` with checkpoint_json NULL -> POST resume -> 404 'no checkpoint to resume from'. A webview that outlived the sidecar shows a forever-pulsing row with frozen cost.
evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:211-215 (CancelledError path writes checkpoint only, no status), :421-438 (shutdown), :185-192/:210/:218 (checkpoint written only on terminal exits, never per round), sidecar/app.py:136-155 (lifespan: no startup sweep; the comment at :149 says runs are cancelled 'FIRST' but they are third), sidecar/services/runs_store.py:6-8 (the zombie is documented as a feature)
notes: Consequence: the store lies about what is running; the one scenario durability exists for (process death) loses the whole transcript. Fix shape: one statement at lifespan startup - UPDATE runs SET status='error', detail='interrupted by sidecar restart' WHERE status='running' - and write the checkpoint inside _on_round_usage (it already writes cost there).

title: Under a light realistic load the sidecar burns ~0.6 of a CPU core continuously, 99% of it on the event-loop (main) thread and mostly between requests, not during them
subsystem: sidecar main process / event loop (background work on an IN-region profile)
repro: L6 soak stack (source sidecar on :52229, copy of the operator data dir, region IN, keyless) driven by soak.py: one 60 s cycle of 8 cheap GETs (watchlist quote batch, one quote/fundamentals/history, portfolio list, two status routes), portfolio CRUD every 10th cycle, one free-model invoke every 15th. Passive `ps -p 64164 -o etime,utime,time`: 8:10.43 CPU at etime 13:41 -> 10:53.62 at 18:13 = 163.2 s CPU in 272 s wall (60%), user 92%; lifetime average 59.8%. `ps -M -p 64164`: first (main) thread 0:50.95 sys + 9:58.70 user = 10:49.65 of 10:53.62; the other 15 threads < 5 s. The soak's requests in those ~4.5 cycles occupy ~12-15 s wall per cycle (~60 s total), so >=100 s of the 163 s CPU fell between requests; decaying %cpu stays 44-62% after all-US cycles whose requests finished in <6 s. Baseline: L1-stranger's clean keyless sidecar idled at 0.0-0.8% CPU.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L6-longsession.md section 5; <scratch>/vysted-iso/soak/soak-mem.jsonl (main.cpu 44.5-66.0 across 15 samples); docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L1-stranger/idle-boot-sampler.jsonl (cpu 0.0-0.8 idle); sidecar/app.py:127-134 (lifespan starts screener warm, fundamentals_warm, nse_symbol_change refresh); sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:199,301,373 (IN-region sweep/bhavcopy/crawl loops); sidecar/main.py:142 (uvicorn.run in the main thread = the asyncio loop thread)
notes: Mechanism not attributed: no profiler was attached (the rule for this stage). The number itself is robust: cumulative CPU time rules out a decaying-average artifact, the user/sys split rules out memory-pressure fault cost, and the per-thread split puts it on the loop thread. Consequence: on the laptop this app targets, the sidecar holds a core at ~60% all session (battery, fans, thermal throttling), and any CPU-bound work on the loop thread adds latency to every async route. Candidates: the IN warm workers, the NSE symbol-change refresh, or post-response work the IN quote/history lanes leave on the loop. fundamentals_cache.db and data_cache.db were not written once in 15 min, which weakens the warm-worker candidates. Confounds: operator data copy rather than a clean profile, source Python rather than the PyInstaller binary, other isolated sidecars on the same IP (Yahoo circuit repeatedly open). Smallest next step: `sample <pid> 10` or `py-spy dump` of the loop thread during an idle gap between soak cycles, then move the hot path off the loop (to_thread) or fix the spinning loop. Stage C re-checks the ≥3 h lifetime average.

refuter.reason: I tried to refute it on four counts and none held. It is not a decaying-%cpu artifact: cumulative CPU time went 8:10.43 -> 10:53.62 over 272 s, a steady 60%. It is not memory-pressure fault cost: 92% is user time. It is not the threadpool running sync handlers: ps -M puts 10:49.65 of 10:53.62 on the main thread, and main.py:142 runs uvicorn (the asyncio loop) there. It is not only request-time work: the soak's requests fill ~60 s of the 272 s window, so at least 100 s of CPU fell between them. A second look found one partial contributor: provider_registry.py:406-407 calls sync provider functions directly on the loop inside async routes (fundamentals.py:89, quotes.py:53/65). That explains loop CPU during requests but not between cycles, so the finding stands with its root cause still unattributed; medium kept (continuous battery/thermal cost on a laptop app, no latency harm yet proven: /health stays 1-8 ms).
